text:
emily-sales: FYI FinServe (dedicated EMEA) is seeing token validation failures after last night's infra upgrade. They're asking for an immediate fix, CSM flagged as P1 and wants an ETA.
joanna: Can you paste a sample error and whether it's causing failed requests or data loss?
emily-sales: sample from support ticket: `ERROR auth: token validation failed: key id mismatch (kms://eu-west-2/finserve)` — customers see 401s intermittently, UX shows "session expired" but no data lost.
sang: I looked quickly — looks like a KMS key rotation and our runtime sometimes picks the old key id from tenant cache. Quick mitigation: force tenants to re-fetch key metadata on auth path. Low-risk patch but requires rolling restarts of dedicated worker for that tenant.
mike: Alternative: short-lived config toggle to enable `allow_kms_fallback` which will try secondary keyserver before failing. Would avoid restarts and could be canaried to the single tenant. Downside: slightly weaker auth path for that tenant until we fully sync keys.
joanna: Tradeoffs noted. Is the fallback implementable without a model restart and without touching customer data plane?
sang: Yes, code change touches auth path only, no model/k8s restart required. We'll need a quick schema flag and rollout guard. Estimated dev + test + canary: ~3 hours.
laura: Security signoff needed for any fallback that weakens auth. Emily, can you confirm FinServe willingness for a temporary fallback and maintenance window?
emily-sales: talking to CSM now — they prefer a canary to their tenant only, no public announcement, and are ok with a 22:00 UTC window tonight.
joanna: OK, proposed plan: 1) implement `allow_kms_fallback` flag (default false), 2) canary rollout scoped to tenant:finserve, 3) monitoring for 30m for 401 rate and latency, 4) if stable promote to tenant-wide 100%, 5) schedule follow-up to remove fallback after key sync.
mike: I pushed a minimal PR branch `auth/kms-fallback` with the feature flag and rollout guard. Quick snippet for rollout config we'll use:```yaml
rollout:
  id: canary-finserve-kms-fallback
  scope: tenant:finserve
  flag: allow_kms_fallback
  target: 10% -> 100% over 10m if healthy
  monitor: errors.401 rate, auth.latency
``` 
laura: I'll start the approval thread with Security (cc @sre). Need signoff by 21:30 UTC to hit 22:00 window.
sang: I'll run unit + integration tests now and prepare canary job. Also preparing a quick smoke script: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://dedicated-eu-west-2/api/v1/auth/test`
opsbot: deploy-bot: canary job created (id: cb-20240321-11), status: pending.
opsbot: deploy-bot: canary started -> target tenant finserve, 10% of their requests.
emily-sales: CSM confirmed maintenance window and OK to use canary-only approach, will notify customer's engineering lead.
opsbot: deploy-bot: canary health after 15m: errors.401 down to baseline, auth.latency unchanged. status: healthy.
joanna: Good. Promote to 100% for tenant only and schedule postmortem doc. Emily, please draft customer comm noting mitigation and follow-up permanency plan.
emily-sales: Draft sent to CSM for review, they'll send to customer after promotion.
opsbot: deploy-bot: canary promoted to 100% for tenant finserve at 22:26 UTC.
laura: Added release-note stub in backlog under "customer fixes" and created follow-up ticket to remove fallback once KMS key metadata fully reconciled.
mike: Will ship production patch to main and schedule patch window to remove fallback after key rotation completes.
joanna: Closing loop: hotpatch path chosen (feature-flagged fallback + tenant canary) instead of full restart hotfix to minimize customer impact. Documenting rollback and monitoring checklist in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
